The following text is from Lilliam Rivera’s 2020 novel Never Look Back. The text describes the narrator’s friend Pheus, a young musician, after finishing a performance during a church service.

Pheus pulls a handkerchief from his back pocket and wipes his forehead. I mime a quiet clap for him. He does a slight bow and flashes his dimples. This is where Pheus [vocab]truly[/vocab] shines. When Pheus is in front of an audience, it’s as if he becomes another person, a more heightened version of himself.

©2020 by Lilliam Rivera
questions.prompt: As used in the text, what does the word “truly” most nearly mean?

explanation.key_evidence: “This is where Pheus [vocab]truly[/vocab] shines.”
explanation.why_correct: In context, “truly” emphasizes that Pheus really shines when performing: he bows, smiles, and becomes “a more heightened version of himself.” Choice C, “Really,” preserves that meaning.
explanation.short: “Truly” means “really” in this context.
explanation.detailed: In context, “truly” emphasizes that Pheus really shines when performing: he bows, smiles, and becomes “a more heightened version of himself.” Choice C, “Really,” preserves that meaning.

choice_analysis.A: “Mildly” would make Pheus shine only slightly, but the passage describes him as especially vivid in front of an audience.
choice_analysis.B: “Scarcely” means hardly or barely, the opposite of the emphasis created by “truly.”
choice_analysis.C: “Really” fits because the sentence says performing is the setting where Pheus genuinely shines.
choice_analysis.D: “Impolitely” describes rude behavior, not the degree or genuineness of Pheus’s performance.

questions.passage: Optimal foraging theory (OFT) holds that animals’ foraging behaviors reflect cost-benefit trade-offs that vary by species and with dynamic ecological circumstances. One such circumstance is lunar intensity, which Mahmoud-Reza Hemami and colleagues found to be negatively associated with foraging by Iranian jerboas but Deborah J. Curtis and colleagues found to be positively associated with foraging by mongoose lemurs. This discrepancy is explicable in terms of OFT: the lemurs’ greater reliance on vision means that higher lunar intensity benefits them more than it benefits the jerboas.
questions.prompt: Information in the text best supports which statement about OFT?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can account for observations of different species responding differently to similar ecological circumstances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It tends to allow for a better understanding of the benefits of ecological circumstances than the costs of those circumstances.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It may be weakened by the finding that the costs and benefits associated with a particular ecological circumstance vary by species.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can explain why some species act in accordance with cost-benefit trade-offs and others do not.

explanation.key_evidence: “This discrepancy is explicable in terms of OFT”
explanation.why_correct: The passage describes two species responding differently to lunar intensity: jerboas forage less, while mongoose lemurs forage more. It then says OFT can explain that discrepancy, supporting the statement that OFT accounts for different species’ different responses to similar circumstances.
explanation.short: OFT can explain different species’ different responses.
explanation.detailed: The passage describes two species responding differently to lunar intensity: jerboas forage less, while mongoose lemurs forage more. It then says OFT can explain that discrepancy, supporting the statement that OFT accounts for different species’ different responses to similar circumstances.

choice_analysis.A: This is supported because the passage says OFT explains opposite responses by two species to lunar intensity.
choice_analysis.B: The passage discusses cost-benefit trade-offs, not that OFT favors understanding benefits over costs.
choice_analysis.C: The passage treats species variation as something OFT explains, not as something that weakens OFT.
choice_analysis.D: The passage says OFT applies to cost-benefit trade-offs generally; it does not divide species into those that follow such trade-offs and those that do not.

questions.passage: A student is writing a research paper on the history of irrigation in the United States, situating the development of Lake Yosemite (created in Merced County, California, in 1888) in a larger historical context. explanation.key_evidence: A contrasts low-humidity southern areas with higher-humidity northern areas.
explanation.why_correct: The claim says California’s climate makes irrigation essential in some parts of the state but not others. Choice A directly supports both parts: low humidity in desert areas makes irrigation required, while higher humidity in northern areas makes it less necessary.
explanation.short: Choice A directly links climate differences to different irrigation needs.
explanation.detailed: The claim says California’s climate makes irrigation essential in some parts of the state but not others. Choice A directly supports both parts: low humidity in desert areas makes irrigation required, while higher humidity in northern areas makes it less necessary.

choice_analysis.A: This quotation matches the claim by tying regional climate differences to whether irrigation is required or less necessary.
choice_analysis.B: This discusses Hohokam irrigation history and engineering, not California climate differences within the state.

questions.passage: Terrestrial plants typically carry a negative electrical charge, while bees and other pollinators tend to accumulate a positive charge. A team of researchers therefore hypothesized that electrostatic attraction (mutual attraction between objects with opposite charges) might enhance pollen transmission between plants and their pollinator species. The team’s experiments showed that the maximum positive charge of wintering honeybees is sufficiently high to facilitate electrostatic pollen transfer, a finding that suggests that ____.
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: red mason bees and houseflies, having greater maximum charges than wintering honeybees have, should not demonstrate this capacity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: houseflies should demonstrate the opposite tendency.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the minimum positive charge necessary for a pollinator to induce electrostatic attraction must be greater than 300 pC.

choices.label: D
choices.text: red mason bees should also demonstrate this capacity.

explanation.short: Red mason bees have a greater maximum charge than honeybees, whose measured charge is already sufficient for pollen transfer.
explanation.key_evidence: The graph shows red mason bees near 780 pC, wintering honeybees near 350 pC, and houseflies near 75 pC.
explanation.why_correct: The text establishes that the honeybees' charge is sufficient. Mason bees have an even greater maximum positive charge, supporting the prediction that they too can attract pollen electrostatically.
explanation.detailed: Use the honeybee observation as evidence of sufficiency, not as a measured minimum requirement. The graph places red mason bees above that sufficient measured value. It does not identify the exact minimum charge or show what a smaller positive charge does, so conclusions about a precise threshold or a reversed effect go beyond the evidence.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. Mason bees should share the capacity rather than lack it, and houseflies have a lower—not greater—maximum charge than honeybees.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. A smaller positive charge does not establish the opposite, repulsive tendency.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. A sufficient observed charge near 350 pC does not prove that the minimum necessary charge exceeds 300 pC.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. The larger positive charge supports predicting the same attraction capacity that the honeybees already demonstrate.

questions.passage: Password strength meters (PSMs) provide real-time feedback to users during the password-creation process about how secure a potential password is. PSMs often include “nudges”—design elements meant to encourage the creation of robust passwords. Other PSMs provide direct guidance on how to create strong passwords. A research team found that the strongest passwords resulted from a combination of these approaches. The team also found that the specific type of nudge (reciprocity, compensation, etc.) did not significantly affect user behavior. It therefore follows that when creating passwords, users receiving _____.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: both compensation and reciprocity nudges would not be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving reciprocity nudges only, although users receiving direct guidance would be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving either type of nudge.

choices.label: B
choices.text: direct guidance would not be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving compensation nudges, although users receiving compensation nudges would be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving reciprocity nudges.

choices.label: C
choices.text: reciprocity nudges would not be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving compensation nudges, although users receiving both direct guidance and reciprocity nudges would be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving only reciprocity nudges.

choices.label: D
choices.text: both direct guidance and reciprocity nudges would not be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving reciprocity nudges only, although users receiving this combination would be expected to create stronger passwords than users receiving both direct guidance and compensation nudges.

Choice C states both ideas by comparing reciprocity with compensation and direct guidance plus reciprocity with reciprocity only.
explanation.short: Choice C matches both findings about nudge type and combined approaches.
explanation.detailed: The findings imply two things: reciprocity and compensation nudges should perform similarly, and combining direct guidance with a nudge should outperform a nudge alone. Choice C states both ideas by comparing reciprocity with compensation and direct guidance plus reciprocity with reciprocity only.

choice_analysis.A: This says direct guidance alone should beat either nudge, but the passage says the strongest passwords came from combining direct guidance with nudges.
choice_analysis.B: This predicts compensation nudges beat reciprocity nudges, contradicting the finding that nudge type did not significantly affect behavior.
choice_analysis.C: This correctly says one nudge type should not outperform another and that direct guidance combined with a nudge should outperform a nudge alone.

explanation.short: The introductory description identifies Elliott, so Elliott must be the subject of the following main clause.
explanation.key_evidence: The opener is 'A politician from South Carolina'; only A continues with Elliott as the clause's subject.
explanation.why_correct: The modifier describes a person, Robert B. Elliott. A attaches it to that person's name and makes Elliott the subject of was elected.
explanation.detailed: Find the grammatical subject of each completed main clause, rather than judging only the next few words. In A it is Elliott, the politician being described. In B it is 1870; in C and D it is his constituents. An introductory time phrase in D does not change that mismatched subject.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. Elliott is the politician described and the subject of was elected.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The main-clause subject 1870 is a year, not the politician named in the modifier.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. Constituents is the subject, making the introductory singular description appear to describe the voters.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. Even after the time phrase in 1870, the main-clause subject remains his constituents rather than Elliott.

questions.passage: The relationship between grassland arthropod populations and agricultural fertilizers containing macronutrients—such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium—was the focus of a 1992 study in the _____ by the researcher Walther van Wingerden, the study examined a variety of arthropod specimens, which had been collected by hand.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.key_evidence: Choice C creates: “...in the Netherlands. Led by... the study examined...”
explanation.why_correct: The text needs a sentence boundary after “Netherlands.” Choice C uses a period, then starts a new sentence with the modifier “Led by the researcher Walther van Wingerden,” correctly attaching that modifier to “the study.”
explanation.short: A period is needed before “Led by...” to avoid a comma splice.
explanation.detailed: The text needs a sentence boundary after “Netherlands.” Choice C uses a period, then starts a new sentence with the modifier “Led by the researcher Walther van Wingerden,” correctly attaching that modifier to “the study.”

choice_analysis.A: “Netherlands and led” does not correctly join the location and modifier and leaves the sentence structure awkward and ungrammatical.
choice_analysis.B: “Netherlands, led” leaves the following independent clause “the study examined...” attached with only commas, producing a comma splice.
choice_analysis.C: This correctly ends the first sentence after “Netherlands” and begins a new sentence with a modifier that describes the study.
choice_analysis.D: “Netherlands led” suggests the Netherlands did the leading and still leaves the following clause improperly joined.

explanation.short: No comma is needed between the title and the name.
explanation.detailed: The phrase “chef and culinary instructor” is a compound title directly identifying Fu Pei-mei before her name. Such a title is not separated from the name by a comma, so choice B is correct.

questions.passage: Anthropologist, activist, and musician Lila Downs draws on a variety of Mexican musical genres in her 2023 album La Sánchez. _____ she draws on corridos, rancheras, and other genres of northern Mexico, even though she is from the southern Mexican city of Oaxaca. “La Sánchez is my contribution,” Downs says in an interview, “as a southern woman, that also considers this music as hers.”
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.key_evidence: The first sentence says Lila Downs draws on “a variety of Mexican musical genres”; the next sentence names corridos, rancheras, and other northern Mexican genres.
explanation.why_correct: “Specifically” signals that the second sentence gives particular examples of the broader musical variety introduced in the first sentence.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. “Specifically” introduces concrete examples of the general category of Mexican musical genres.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “Therefore” would show a result, but the second sentence is not caused by the first; it provides examples.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “In conclusion” would signal a summary or ending, but the passage is adding detail.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “Rather” would correct or contrast with the prior claim, but the second sentence supports it.

explanation.short: The second sentence names specific genres after the first sentence mentions a variety of genres.
explanation.detailed: Because corridos and rancheras are examples of the Mexican musical genres mentioned earlier, the blank needs a transition that introduces specifics.

questions.passage: The World Cup of men’s soccer, one of the biggest sporting events on the planet, brought 32 national teams from six continents to the host country, Germany, in 2006. _____ only 16 teams, all from Europe and the Americas, competed in the 1958 World Cup in Sweden.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.key_evidence: The 2006 World Cup had 32 national teams from six continents, while the 1958 World Cup had only 16 teams from Europe and the Americas.
explanation.why_correct: “In contrast” accurately marks the difference between the larger, more geographically diverse 2006 tournament and the smaller 1958 tournament.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “Therefore” would signal a result, but the 1958 tournament is not a consequence of the 2006 tournament.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “For instance” would introduce an example of the prior idea, but the 1958 World Cup contrasts with the 2006 World Cup.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. “In contrast” directly signals the difference between the two tournaments.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “In other words” would restate the same idea, but the second sentence gives different facts.

explanation.short: The sentence contrasts the 2006 and 1958 World Cups.
explanation.detailed: The second sentence gives smaller numbers and a narrower geographic range than the first sentence, so a contrast transition is required.

questions.passage: Broadcasting from the Yankton Sioux Tribe’s lands in southern South Dakota, the Native-run radio station KDKO 89.5 FM does much to serve the local Dakota-speaking community. _____ it broadcasts local news and music as well as programming in the Dakota language.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.key_evidence: The first sentence says KDKO “does much to serve” the Dakota-speaking community; the next sentence lists local news, music, and Dakota-language programming.
explanation.why_correct: “Specifically” introduces concrete examples of how the station serves that community.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “Instead” would signal replacement or contrast, but the broadcasts are examples of how KDKO serves the community.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. “Specifically” introduces the listed services as examples of the station’s work.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “As a result” would show an effect, but the broadcasts are not a result of the prior sentence; they explain it.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “Nevertheless” would introduce a contrast, but the second sentence supports the first.

explanation.short: The second sentence lists specific services KDKO provides.
explanation.detailed: The passage moves from a general statement about serving the community to examples of that service, so “Specifically” is the best transition.

questions.passage: In the West African country of Sierra Leone, the percentage of the population living in cities rose from 40.8% to 42.9% between 2015 and 2020. _____ urbanization rates climbed across West Africa as a whole, rising 3.2 percentage points in that five-year period.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.key_evidence: Sierra Leone’s urban population percentage rose between 2015 and 2020, and urbanization rates across West Africa also climbed in that same five-year period.
explanation.why_correct: “Concurrently” means at the same time, which fits two urbanization trends occurring during the same period.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “In other words” would restate the Sierra Leone statistic, but the second sentence gives a related regional trend.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “Eventually” would emphasize a later outcome, but both trends are described over the same 2015-2020 period.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. “Concurrently” shows that the Sierra Leone trend and the regional West Africa trend happened during the same period.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “For example” would make West Africa an example of Sierra Leone, but the second sentence broadens from one country to the region.

explanation.short: Both urbanization increases happened during the same five-year period.
explanation.detailed: The blank needs a transition that links simultaneous trends, not a contrast or example.

questions.passage: Al-Andalus, the historical region of the Iberian Peninsula that includes most of modern-day Spain, was ruled by various Arabic-speaking Muslim states between the eighth and fifteenth centuries. _____ many Arabic words, such as “alacrán”—meaning “scorpion”—made their way into the Spanish language.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.key_evidence: Al-Andalus was ruled by Arabic-speaking Muslim states for centuries, and many Arabic words later entered Spanish.
explanation.why_correct: “Consequently” shows the cause-and-effect relationship: Arabic-speaking rule helps explain why Arabic words became part of Spanish.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. “Consequently” signals that Arabic words entering Spanish was a result of the Arabic-speaking rule described in the first sentence.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “Specifically” would narrow a broad category already named, but the first sentence gives historical context rather than a category of words.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “For example” would make the second sentence an example of the first sentence, but it is better understood as a result of the historical situation.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “Instead” would signal replacement or contrast, and the second sentence does not contradict the first.

explanation.short: Arabic words entering Spanish is presented as a result of Arabic-speaking rule in Al-Andalus.
explanation.detailed: Because the second sentence follows from the historical rule described in the first, a cause-and-effect transition is needed.

questions.passage:

• Studies of Iberian orcas suggest recent increases in tuna populations have reduced the time the orcas spend hunting by 99%.
• Researchers believe this shift has increased the number of interactions between marine vessels and understimulated orcas.
• The workshop advised mariners to avoid orcas pending further testing of the efficacy of TAST, a harmless acoustic deterrent.
questions.prompt: The student wants to make and support a claim about Iberian orca behavior. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The recent destructive behavior of Iberian orcas may be the result of understimulation, given that orcas’ interactions with marine vessels have increased as the orcas have spent less time hunting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tuna populations have increased by approximately 99% off the Iberian Peninsula due to changes in the hunting behavior of Iberian orcas.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As supported by the workshop’s analysis of 637 encounters between vessels and Iberian orcas, TAST is a harmless and effective acoustic deterrent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In 2024, Spain and Portugal sponsored a workshop that addressed incidents where pods of Iberian orcas were ramming, nudging, or biting the rudders of vessels.

explanation.short: A proposes understimulation as a reason for the destructive behavior and supports it with reduced hunting time.
explanation.key_evidence: The notes connect a 99% reduction in hunting time to increased interactions between vessels and understimulated orcas.
explanation.why_correct: The student needs both a behavioral claim and support. A states a cautious cause for the behavior and cites the corresponding hunting-time change from the notes.
explanation.detailed: Distinguish what increased by what amount: tuna became more plentiful, and hunting time fell by 99%. Researchers link that change to understimulation and more vessel interactions. The acoustic deterrent's effectiveness remains under testing. A accurately combines the behavioral hypothesis and its support without overstating it.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. This states the understimulation hypothesis and supports it with the reduction in hunting time alongside increased vessel interactions.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The 99% figure describes the reduction in hunting time, not an increase in tuna populations; the claimed causal direction is also reversed.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The notes call TAST harmless but say its efficacy awaits further testing, so effective is not yet supported.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The workshop and damage are accurately described, but this gives event context without a supported explanatory claim about the behavior.

choice_analysis.C: Correct. “Influenced” precisely means shaped or affected by her group experience and interests.

questions.passage: It would not be productive for supporters of a proposal to increase the toll that drivers must pay to use the Veterans Bridge, which spans the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River in Virginia, to direct their arguments at those drivers who strongly believe that the current toll is too high. choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “Ignore” means pay no attention to someone, but the sentence is about directing arguments at them.

explanation.short: “Sway” means persuade or influence someone.
explanation.detailed: The phrase “whose mind is already made up” shows that supporters would be trying to change an already fixed opinion.

questions.passage: Many studies have found a positive association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury in bodies of fresh water undisturbed by human activity. choice_analysis.A: Correct. It accounts for the fact that the studies were conducted in different countries and environments.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The text does not say both carbon and mercury are much higher in wastewater-impacted water.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The text does not compare how common wastewater and mining disturbances are.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The text identifies one Laos study and one US study but does not compare how common wastewater-impacted bodies are in the two countries.

explanation.short: The differing study locations could explain the differing results.
explanation.detailed: The final sentence points to Laos versus the United States, so the logical conclusion concerns underlying environmental differences.

questions.passage: Many folktales that originate in the Lithuanian language begin with the same phrase. In English, this phrase _____ roughly to “beyond nine seas, beyond nine lagoons.”

questions.passage: You can see Brazilian artist Tarsila do Amaral’s bold use of color in her painting Sol Poente (Setting Sun). Created in 1929, the painting ____ bright green cacti towering in front of a candy-orange sky.

questions.passage: The Eiger, the Mönch, the Jungfrau—Alpine summits like these were little more than wastelands to many Europeans until the eighteenth century, when attitudes toward such intimidating landscapes shifted as part of a broader aesthetic ____ by Irish philosopher Edmund Burke, this shift framed mountains as sublime objects capable of producing delightful terror.

questions.passage: While some researchers have identified the planet Teegarden’s Star c as potentially habitable, it’s unlikely that humanity will be able to take advantage of its favorable conditions anytime soon—it’s 12.58 light years away. ____ at 1,196 light years away, the planet Kepler-1410b is also inaccessible.

questions.passage: John Rankin was an outspoken abolitionist whose Ohio home was a stop on the underground railroad (the network of people and places that some enslaved people used to escape to freedom). _____ supporters of the railroad were secretive about their antislavery views.
